3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of large extent of lands situated at Ariyankuppam Village, Puducherry,
measuring 13.59.50 Hectares = 33.58 Acres under Sale Deed dated 17.06.2022.
Based on the initial request made by the Archaeological Survey of India, the Government of Puducherry has proposed to acquire the entire extent of lands from the Petitioner.

However, after detailed study and analysing,
the Government of Puducherry had issued Notification under Section 4(1) dated 25.07.2003 and Declaration U/s.6 dated 26.09.2003 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and acquired only an extent of 8.88.40 Hectares = 21.92 Acres(out of the total 13.59.50 Hectares =33.58 Acres).

Based on the same, LAO had passed an Award, determined compensation, took possession and handed over the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/09/2025 06:19:19 pm ) lands to Archaeological Survey of India.

However, as the compensation was not correctly determined, the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court vide Judgment and Decree dated 19.11.2024 made in A.S.No.237/2018 had M.R.Somu Alias Munien vs The Govt.Of Puducherry on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177874601/

2 directed the LAO to redetermine the compensation in accordance with the ancient monuments &
Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 and the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

3.1.Further, he would submit that after the above acquisition proceedings, out of the total extent of 33.58 Acres, an extent of 11.66 Acres is remaining with the petitioner and he is continuing as its absolute owner and possessor.
The Revenue Department had also measured, demarcated the remaining lands, sub-divided and assigned sub-division numbers and issued Patta No.887 to the petitioner.
During the initial proposal for acquisition proceedings, the Guideline Register Value of all the lands of the petitioner was entered as Zero in the Guideline Value Register.

After the acquisition was completed, the Revenue Department ought to have removed the entry of Zero and fixed the Guideline Register Value for the remaining lands in accordance with the prevailing market value.
But they https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/09/2025 06:19:19 pm ) failed to do so.

Hence, the petitioner submitted application dated 15.06.2022 followed by another application 04.01.2023 in a prescribed Form and various oral representations to the 2nd respondent requesting them to remove the entry of Zero in the Guideline Register and fix Guideline Register Value for his lands.
Since no action has been taken on the said representation, the petitioner is before this Court by way of the present Writ Petition.

4. The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents on instructions would submit that the respondents will take action of the application of the petitioner dated 04.01.2023 on merits and in accordance with law, within a stipulated period.

5. Heard both sides.
6.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and having regard to the submissions made,
without going into the merits of the case, this Court directs the respondent concerned to pass orders on the application https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/09/2025 06:19:19 pm ) of the petitioner dated 04.01.2023, on merits and in accordance with law, after issuing notice to the petitioner and also affording due opportunity of hearing to the petitioner as well as to any of the interested parties, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and communicate the decision taken to the petitioner.
7.
With the above directions, this writ petition is disposed of.
No costs.
